voiceover: Philippians 2 carries one of the oldest songs of the church. The one every knee will honor first emptied himself — he took the form of a servant and was obedient to death on a cross. Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord. But those are borrowed words. Paul is reaching back centuries, to Isaiah 45 — one of the most fiercely monotheistic texts in all of Scripture. There the LORD declares, 'I am God, and there is no other,' and swears that to him every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear. It is worship owed to the one God of Israel, and to no one else. And Paul takes that very text — the honor YHWH claims for himself alone — and applies it to Jesus. The name Jesus receives is the divine name itself: Kyrios, the Lord. Jesus is placed inside the identity of the one God, receiving the worship and the name that belong to YHWH alone. And monotheism stays intact — it is all to the glory of God the Father. One God. And Jesus is Lord.
